previous_revision.note: cases-r2.json and the run 1 result files stay as they were. This revision changes one thing in the checks (Amendment 4) and records new expectations for the second run.

frozen_questions.note: The six frozen questions are unchanged and the file is untouched. This revision pins how each question is executed, so a result can be read against a fixed operational meaning.

threat_model.primary: honest-but-confused relay. It authenticates its upstream peer correctly and never signs anything it believes false. It can be confused: it picks which held binding to forward by route instead of by caller, it can fire a held binding from a retry queue after the session that supplied it has ended, and it can route to the wrong downstream agent.
threat_model.supplementary: malicious relay. It holds a valid relay key and signs whatever it chooses. Run only as case S1, reported separately, and excluded from the frozen verdict.

arms.direct: The caller reaches the downstream agent with no intermediary. The downstream check is the A2A-MCP-CROSSING-001 bound check, line for line, plus one addition: the current status of the request-authority record is read from a status registry rather than a single harness flag, so case 6 can say exactly what was revoked. Amendment 4 adds one comparison: the identity of the receiving downstream agent must equal mandate.executor_id, the same comparison added to the 001 check in commit 098e97a. It runs after the request_id comparison and before the mandate adapter, as in 001.
arms.brokered_native: Reference only. The relay authenticates downstream as itself and forwards the task. No binding is checked. Mirrors the 001 native arm. Unchanged by Amendment 4: this reference arm checks nothing, so it gains no executor comparison.
arms.brokered_a2: The design frozen by AMENDMENT-2.md. A bare relay claim in A2A extension metadata names the relay and the requester it says it carries for. The downstream compares the presenting identity with the named relay and the claimed requester with mandate.requester_id, then runs the 001 checks. Nothing verifies the claim. An honest-but-confused relay fills the claimed requester from the binding it forwards, which is the naive build the earlier amendments described. Amendment 4 adds one comparison: the identity of the receiving downstream agent must equal mandate.executor_id, the same comparison added to the 001 check in commit 098e97a. It runs after the request_id comparison and before the mandate adapter, as in 001.
arms.brokered_a3: The design defined by AMENDMENT-3.md. A2A extension metadata carries a digest-bound reference to a separate relay attestation, signed by the relay with a registered key. The attestation binds relay_id, upstream_peer (the identity the relay authenticated), requester_id, task_id, context_id, action_digest, downstream (the agent the relay is calling), validity window, nonce and mandate_digest. The downstream checks the digest, the signature, every bound field, and then runs the 001 checks. Amendment 4 adds one comparison: the identity of the receiving downstream agent must equal mandate.executor_id, the same comparison added to the 001 check in commit 098e97a. It runs after the request_id comparison and before the mandate adapter, as in 001.

verdict_rules.per_design: Computed separately for brokered_a2 and brokered_a3, against direct. Neither design is chosen after the fact.
verdict_rules.void: valid_brokered_crossing fails in direct or in the design being judged.
verdict_rules.interesting: at least one non-supplementary mutation is refused in direct and takes effect in the design being judged.
verdict_rules.refuted: every non-supplementary mutation refused in direct is also refused in the design being judged.
verdict_rules.fourth_outcome: a mutation refused in the design but taking effect in direct is reported as the intermediary doing enforcement work.
verdict_rules.shared_gap: a mutation that takes effect in direct and in the design is reported as a gap the broker inherits from direct.

measure: Whether the MCP tool was invoked for the mutated crossing. A refusal after the effect counts as the effect taking place.
replay: Each case starts with fresh nonce state. Durable replay protection remains a deployment condition and is outside this run.
notClaimed: That any named gateway or product behaves like these arms.
That A2A, MCP or any gateway is defective.
That the relay attestation shape is a proposal for any specification. It is a construct for this experiment.

cases.prediction: succeed in every arm. If it fails in direct, brokered_a2 or brokered_a3, that design is void.

expectation_at_amendment_4.note: Same as run 1, with the same refusal reasons. The new comparison runs after every check that refused this case in run 1, and the receiving agent here is agent-b, which the mandate names.

cases.role: designed negative control in brokered_a2; open question in brokered_a3

cases.direct: agent-c presents agent-a's binding to agent-b directly.
cases.brokered: agent-c, separately authenticated, submits on the same route. The confused relay forwards the binding it holds for that route, which is agent-a's.
cases.expectation_at_amendment_3: brokered_a2: takes effect, by design, because nothing checks the claimed requester against who called the relay (Takao Sato is right that this was a designed negative control). brokered_a3: refused, if and only if the honest relay's upstream_peer of agent-c reaches the downstream comparison. direct: refused. brokered_native: takes effect.

expectation_at_amendment_4.note: Same as run 1, with the same refusal reasons. The new comparison runs after every check that refused this case in run 1, and the receiving agent here is agent-b, which the mandate names.

cases.reading: A genuine, correctly signed, unexpired, unused binding issued by agent-a for this exact action, which reached the relay outside this exchange (a retry queue firing after the session ended). No caller submits anything in this exchange.
cases.direct: The relay identity presents that binding to agent-b directly.
cases.brokered: The relay calls agent-b as itself. brokered_a2: the claim copies agent-a from the binding. brokered_a3: the honest relay has no authenticated upstream peer, so it signs upstream_peer as itself.
cases.expectation_at_amendment_3: direct refused; brokered_a2 takes effect; brokered_a3 refused; brokered_native takes effect.

expectation_at_amendment_4.note: Same as run 1, with the same refusal reasons. The new comparison runs after every check that refused this case in run 1, and the receiving agent here is agent-b, which the mandate names.

cases.reading: The other plausible reading of case 4: the binding is fabricated at the relay and carries no valid mandate signature.
cases.direct: The relay identity presents the fabricated binding directly.
cases.brokered: The relay presents the fabricated binding with its claim or attestation.
cases.expectation_at_amendment_3: refused wherever a mandate signature is checked (direct, brokered_a2, brokered_a3). Mandate signatures in the 001 harness are modelled, so this case measures the check order and says nothing new about cryptography.

expectation_at_amendment_4.note: Same as run 1, with the same refusal reasons. The new comparison runs after every check that refused this case in run 1, and the receiving agent here is agent-b, which the mandate names.

cases.direct: agent-a presents its binding, which names executor agent-b, to agent-d.
cases.brokered: The relay routes agent-a's request to agent-d. The honest relay names agent-d as downstream in its attestation, because that is where it is calling.
cases.expectation_at_amendment_3: takes effect in every arm. Read before building: the 001 check never compares the receiving agent with mandate.executor_id, and the attestation's downstream field only proves where the relay called. If this holds, the gap belongs to the 001 check and travels into 002 unchanged.

expectation_at_amendment_4.note: Changed from Amendment 3. agent-d receives a binding whose mandate names agent-b, so the new comparison refuses it in direct, brokered_a2 and brokered_a3 with 'executor identity substitution'. In brokered_a3 the attestation names agent-d truthfully and passes its own downstream check first; the refusal comes from the new comparison. brokered_native still checks nothing.

cases.brokered: agent-a submits; the record is revoked; the relay dispatches as itself.
cases.expectation_at_amendment_3: refused in direct, brokered_a2 and brokered_a3, if the downstream reads current record status; takes effect in brokered_native.

cases.brokered: agent-a submits; the mandate is revoked; the relay dispatches.

cases.revoked: agent-a's transport credential: its Keycloak session is ended and the access token introspects inactive. The request-authority record and mandate stay live.
cases.direct: agent-a's session is ended, then agent-a calls agent-b with the same access token.
cases.brokered: agent-a submits while its token is live; the session is ended; the relay dispatches as itself.
cases.must: be refused, if transport credential revocation is meant to end authority
cases.expectation_at_amendment_3: takes effect in every arm. Downstream token checks are offline JWKS signature checks, and in brokered arms the downstream never sees agent-a's token. Recorded so the result is read as a statement about which revocation reaches the crossing, rather than as a gap only in brokers.

expectation_at_amendment_4.note: Unchanged and still a gap. Amendment 4 does nothing about revocation of the transport credential. The downstream still checks tokens offline against JWKS, and behind a relay it never sees agent-a's token.

cases.role: supplementary mutation under the malicious relay model; excluded from the frozen verdict
cases.direct: agent-c presents agent-a's binding to agent-b directly.
cases.brokered: agent-c submits; the relay knowingly forwards agent-a's held binding and signs upstream_peer agent-a.
cases.expectation_at_amendment_3: direct refused; brokered_a2 and brokered_a3 take effect. A relay-signed attestation cannot outvote its own signer. Closing this needs evidence the relay cannot produce alone, such as a caller-signed handoff naming the relay, the downstream and the nonce.

expectation_at_amendment_4.note: Unchanged. The relay routes to agent-b, the executor the mandate names, so the new comparison passes and the false upstream_peer still gets through brokered_a2 and brokered_a3.
